# hvir

A lightweight, view-first workbench for agentic development.

hvir is an Electron desktop application that brings terminals, agent sessions, git, and
document review into a single fast workspace. It is built around a view-first philosophy:
the UI projects live state from authoritative main-process/worker services, so the
renderer stays a thin, recoverable presentation layer.

## Features

- **Terminal workspaces** — GPU-accelerated terminal rendering via
  [ghostty-web](https://github.com/jarmak-personal/ghostty-web) backed by `node-pty`,
  with split panes, search, semantic navigation, themes, clipboard integration, and
  session recovery.
- **Agent session management** — launch and observe agent harnesses (e.g. Claude,
  Codex) with profiles, telemetry, usage tracking, and a sessions overview.
- **Git integration** — workspace status, graph layout, commit details, diffs, blame,
  staging, and guarded mutations executed in dedicated worker hosts.
- **Remote workspaces over SSH** — connect to remote hosts with SSH config parsing,
  host trust/identity management, and transport pooling.
- **Document viewing & review** — markdown rendering (with Mermaid diagrams and
  syntax highlighting via Shiki), CodeMirror-based source and merge views, and a
  document-review workflow.
- **Multi-project workbench** — a project registry with drag organization, watchers,
  per-project workspaces, and attention/activity indicators.
- **Diagnostics & health** — built-in diagnostic reporting with evidence masking and
  workbench health monitoring.

## Tech stack

- **Electron 43** with **electron-vite** (main / preload / renderer / workers)
- **React 19** + TypeScript renderer
- **ghostty-web**, **node-pty**, **ssh2**, **CodeMirror 6**, **markdown-it**,
  **Mermaid**, **Shiki**
- **Vitest** (+ Stryker mutation testing), **ESLint**, **Prettier**

## Requirements

- Node.js **>= 24**
- macOS (arm64) and Linux (x64/arm64) packaging targets

## Getting started

```sh
npm install        # also rebuilds native modules (node-pty) via postinstall
npm run dev        # start in development mode
```

## Common scripts

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Run the app in development mode |
| `npm run build` | Typecheck and build with electron-vite |
| `npm test` / `npm run test:watch` | Run the Vitest suite |
| `npm run lint` / `npm run format` | Lint / format the codebase |
| `npm run typecheck` | Typecheck node and web tsconfigs |
| `npm run verify` | Full local gate: seams, ADRs, architecture, lint, typecheck, tests |
| `npm run smoke` | Build in smoke mode and run smoke scenarios |
| `npm run pack:mac:arm64` | Package a macOS (arm64) `.pkg` |
| `npm run pack:linux:x64` / `:arm64` | Package a Linux `.deb` |

See `package.json` for the full list, including SSH acceptance tests, release
assembly, and project-management tooling.

## Project structure

```
src/
  main/       Electron main process: PTY, git, SSH, sessions, IPC authority
  preload/    Preload bridges
  renderer/   React UI (terminal, viewer, git, sessions, settings, workbench)
  shared/     Types and contracts shared across processes
  workers/    Worker hosts (e.g. git engine)
packages/
  rename-noreplace/  Native helper for no-replace renames
scripts/      Build, release, smoke, architecture, and project-management tooling
test/         Vitest unit/integration tests
```

## Contributing

- Run `npm run hooks:install` to install the git hooks in `.githooks/`.
- Before opening a PR, run `npm run verify` — it enforces architecture seams,
  ADR checks, lint, typecheck, and the test suite.
- Architectural decisions are recorded as ADRs and checked with `npm run check-adrs`.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). See [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for bundled
third-party licenses.
